findings.failureScenario: missing_count treats the cache as stale whenever catalog.revision differs, and revision increments on every applied op, including Op::SetDevelop. While a slider is dragged (an op per change) each finished scan is immediately followed by another: the UI thread collects every library photo's path (missing::candidates) and a new worker thread stats every original file. On a 100k-photo library, or one on a network share, this is a continuous stat storm for the whole editing session, duplicating the cached Availability probe the app already has. The documented 'at most every 5 s' bound only applies when the revision is unchanged.
findings.action: Debounce the revision-triggered refresh (minimum interval regardless of revision, e.g. 5 s) or derive the count from session.media.availability instead of re-statting; avoid cloning all paths on the UI thread.

findings.failureScenario: The NewSmartAlbum dialog calls catalog.query(&rules, ...) (a full-library filter) and rebuilds filter_label on every frame the dialog is shown, uncached. The Edit smart album dialog uses Caches::rules_view keyed on revision and rules precisely to avoid this. With a large library every pointer move or keystroke while the dialog is open re-scans all photos, making the name field laggy.
findings.action: Route the count through Caches::rules_view (or key a cache on revision and rules) as the edit dialog does.

findings.failureScenario: The RenameKeyword dialog scans every photo and every keyword (is_under) each frame just to show a count. Cost is O(photos x keywords) per frame while typing in the field on a large library.
findings.action: Compute the count once per catalog revision and keyword (cache like Caches::keyword_ticks) instead of per frame.

findings.failureScenario: Every Caches entry (counts, filter_values, date_groups, folder_tree, keyword_tree, people, album counts) is keyed on cat.revision, which Catalog::apply bumps for every op, including Op::SetDevelop applied during slider drags. Panels that are visible then recompute their O(N) library scans per drag step: counts walks all photos, filter_values clones and sorts every camera and lens string, date_groups and trees rebuild. Edits that cannot affect these aggregates still flush them, so editing a photo in a large library costs several full scans per frame.
findings.action: Key aggregate caches on a metadata/membership revision that develop-only ops do not bump, or skip invalidation for ops that touch only develop settings.
